text:
“Ronaldinho played for Ravenna, in Serie C, earlier this month. It was his first professional appearance in more than 11 years,” writes George Jones. “Have any other footballers had long career hiatuses? And has any player had a longer hiatus than 11 years?”
Ronaldinho’s last professional appearance before his return for Ravenna came on 26 September 2015 for Fluminense, who won 2-0 at home against Goiás. He was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Fans of symmetry will be pleased to see that 11 years and 50 days later, the Brazilian returned for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against another team with five letters and an accent in their name, Forlì, and was withdrawn after 45 minutes.
Considering he is now 46 and was playing against a team containing a couple of players 26 years his junior, his 25 touches, one key pass (in the buildup to the opening goal) and 81% passing accuracy in a single half is better than respectable. And nope, stats weren’t available for tracking back and we don’t imagine he ranked too highly on that metric … but he’s 46! Only time will tell if the World Cup winner plays again. “It was amazing,” he beamed after the match. “I got more than 30 minutes under my belt and feel good. I didn’t really want to come off. It was all over in a flash. I’m still not sure if this will be my only appearance, but if the president comes calling, I’ll be back.”
But back to the question. There have been a few high-profile returns following a player’s initial “retirement”. In 2012 Paul Scholes jumped back into Manchester United’s midfield seven months after hanging up his boots to help out amid an injury crisis and played for another 18 months, helping United to seal their 20th league title in May 2013. Arjen Robben resumed his career at his boyhood club, Groningen, a year after calling time at Bayern Munich.
A more curious example is that of the former Argentina goalkeeper Carlos Roa, who at his peak and aged 30, took a retreat from football to focus on his faith with reports suggesting he anticipated the year 2000 being the end of the world. A devout Christian, Roa went to live with his family in a secluded area of Argentina to prepare for the apocalypse. When it didn’t come, he resumed his career at Mallorca a year after his last appearance but never played for the national team again.
But these tales get us nowhere near to Ronaldinho. Gareth Barry had a four-and-a-half-year hiatus between his retirement as a professional at West Brom in 2020 and his return to playing again at Hurstpierpoint in the Mid Sussex League Championship in February 2025 – not at professional level but still pretty competitive. Jürgen Klinsmann made a similar return to playing at amateur level five years after “retiring”. Klinsmann scored on his farewell appearance for Tottenham in a 1-1 draw with Southampton on the last day of the 1997-98 Premier League season. However, aged 39, he came back under the pseudonym “Jay Göppingen” and scored five goals in eight appearances for Orange County Blue Star, a team in the Premier Development League (then the fourth tier of the US pyramid).
Maybe Ronaldinho was inspired by his former World Cup-winning teammate Denílson signing for Íbis Sport Club in 2022, 12 years after his retirement. However, the then 44-year-old never made an appearance for the lower-league Brazilian club, with the signing seemingly a publicity stunt for a club often dubbed the “worst in the world” after going three years, 11 months and 26 days without a win in the 1980s.
Which takes us to another brilliant Brazilian. The late, great Sócrates came out of retirement on 20 November 2004 aged 50, 15 years after his last appearance for Botafogo on 12 November 1989. He signed a one-month player-coach deal with Garforth Town, on the outskirts of Leeds, in the Northern Counties East Football League and played 12 minutes at the end of a 2-2 draw with Tadcaster Albion. “It was far too cold; the second I got out there I had an incredible headache. I’m just not used to it,” he gasped after the match. “But I really enjoyed it and it was an interesting experience.” His appearance drew huge crowds to tiny Wheatley Park and came about because of a shared interest in football coaching schools for children which the owner, Simon Clifford, was trying to promote.
The hiatus for Sócrates stands at 15 years and eight days, four years greater than that of Ronaldinho, though perhaps Ronaldinho’s ability to step back into the third tier of a professional league and more than hold his own is a more impressive achievement. What is unarguable, though, is their status as two Brazil greats.
The former Scotland defender Neil McBain had a playing hiatus longer than the two legends above, however. “McBain started his career as a half-back for Ayr United in 1915,” writes Robin Horton. “He retired in 1931, as player-manager for Watford, by which time he was playing centre-half, his last game being an FA Cup tie at Birmingham on 14 February. By 1946 he was in charge of New Brighton.”
“On 15 March 1947, with the club suffering a goalkeeping crisis, and with four players – including chosen keeper Corbett – failing to turn up for a match at Hartlepool United, McBain himself donned the green jersey. The Rakers duly lost 3–0, although the first goal was a shot ‘which might easily have caused Frank Swift’s eyes to boggle’. At 51 years old, he was the oldest player ever to play in the Football League – 16 years, one month and one day from his previous appearance.”
Drawing down
“Are Leicester City the quickest team ever to go from winning the FA Cup to playing in the FA Cup first round proper?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.
Leicester won the FA Cup in 2021, when Youri Tielemans scored a spectacular winner against Chelsea at Wembley in front of a post-Covid crowd of 20,000. As any fule kno, they’re now in League One after back-to-back relegations. That meant an early start in the FA Cup: on 6 November, to be precise, when Leicester won 4-2 at Oxford City.
They’re not the first team to plunge from winners to first-round entrants in the space of five years, though. As Rhys Shakeshaft points out, until 1925 the winners began their defence in the first round as a matter of course. That included Tottenham Hotspur, who won the competition as a non-league team in 1901.
Since 1925, when the top clubs were first given a bye to the third round, two teams have suffered a faster descent than Leicester.
“Portsmouth won the FA Cup in 2008,” writes Michael Haughey, “and dropped into League One in 2012 four seasons later.” But, as Alicia Butteriss and others point out, Wigan went from champions to first-round entrants in half that time.
They famously beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final of 2013, the same year in which they were relegated from the Premier League. Two years later, they dropped another level into League One. On 7 November 2015, precisely 910 days after Wigan beat City at Wembley, they played Bury away in the first round. Bury won 4-0.
Knowledge archive
“Is the incident involving CSKA Sofia and Levski Sofia the first time a match has ever been delayed by a snowball fight?” wondered Nathan Fisher in 2014.
Nope, it isn’t Nathan. On 19 December 2010, Larissa fans took advantage of a rare snowfall in Greece to hurl missiles at Olympiakos’s Vasilis Torosidis, now of Roma of course. Went down like a sack of potatoes. On the same day in Belgium, Anderlecht’s Jonathan Legear and Mbark Boussoufa came under heavy fire from Club Brugge fans with the referee forced to take the players back to the dressing room for seven minutes before the game restarted. Anderlecht went on to beat their rivals 2-0, with Legear pelting his own fans in celebration, much to the displeasure of a Club Brugge steward who shoved the Belgian player. This is the footballer, remember, who caused £240,000 worth of damage crashing his Porsche into a petrol station in 2012. He’s currently a free agent and being linked with Blackpool. Gulp!
In 2012, the Dynamo Moscow striker Zvjezdan Misimovic received a suspended one-match league ban and a £1,300 fine for kicking snowballs at Spartak Moscow supporters during his warm-up, or “provocative acts that created a threat of starting disturbances in the stadium” according to the Russian Football Union. Spartak fans responded in kind.
Can you help?
“Sunderland have six away games in December. Is this a festive record?” asks Masai Graham.
“If West Ham fail to get out of the Championship and Manchester United and Manchester City end up there next season (albeit by different methods), we’ll be looking at three second-tier clubs with a combined average attendance of around 175,000,” writes Daz Pearce. “Would this be the highest-attended second tier of all time?”
“The top seven teams in the standings of the Dutch Eredivisie are separated by one point between each position respectively,” notes Michiel Pauw. “Has there ever been a longer list of positions where this has occurred? Or perhaps later in the season?”
“Manchester United were two goals (and a man) down within the opening 15 minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s managerial debut, but which manager has endured the worst first quarter-of-an-hour in a job?” queries David Hagan.
“During the Manchester City v Fulham game, the commentator said “Berge … King”, without acknowledging how funny that was,” emails Phil Grey. “What other passes from one player to another have there been that are humorous?”
- Mail us with all of your questions and answers
digest_he:
רונאלדיניו חזר למגרשים המקצועניים ושיחק במדי קבוצת רוונה מהליגה השלישית באיטליה, בגיל 46 וזאת לאחר הפסקה של יותר מ-11 שנים מאז משחקו המקצועני האחרון במדי פלומיננסה. למרות גילו, הופעתו במחצית המשחק זכתה למחמאות על רקע היכולת והנתונים שהציג על המגרש.

עם זאת, הוא אינו השחקן היחיד שחזר לשחק לאחר הפסקה ארוכה או שפרש וחזר. שחקנים בולטים כמו פול סקולס ואריאן רובן חזרו מפרישה כדי לעזור לקבוצותיהם, בעוד שחקנים אחרים רשמו הפסקות ארוכות יותר מסיבות אישיות או דתיות, כמו השוער קרלוס רואה שפרש כדי להתמקד באמונתו.

בין המקרים הבולטים ניתן למצוא את האגדה הברזילאית סוקרטס, שחזר לשחק באופן חד-פעמי בגיל 50 לאחר הפסקה של 15 שנים. כמו כן, השוער הסקוטי ניל מקביין שיחק משחק רשמי בגיל 51 לאחר הפסקה של 16 שנים עקב משבר שוערי קבוצתו.
